title: TVS Electronics Ltd - 532513 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: TVS Electronics Q4 FY26 consolidated EBITDA margin rose to 5.96% (+413 bps YoY) on revenue of about Rs 117 crore, while FY26 revenue grew only about 6%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue from operations was about Rs 117 crore, up 2% YoY and 3% QoQ, with EBITDA of about Rs 7 crore and PAT of about Rs 3 crore. For FY26, revenue was about Rs 455 crore (up about 6%), EBITDA about Rs 20 crore (up 77%) and PAT about Rs 1 crore versus a Rs 4 crore loss in FY25. Management attributed margin gains to product mix and TCM (cost control) initiatives, and said it is deliberately exiting low-margin orders, which slowed top-line growth. Working capital rose, lifting debt-to-equity from 0.34x to 0.43x.

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated revenue from operations Q4 FY26

financial_highlights.change: +233% YoY, +8% QoQ; margin +413 bps YoY, +24 bps QoQ
PAT margin +300 bps YoY, +212 bps QoQ
vs loss of about Rs 4 crore in FY25; PAT margin +120 bps
spiked QoQ; management said it is routine forex forward mark-to-market

segments.name: Products and Solutions Group (PSG)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue about Rs 80 crore, up 2% QoQ on higher volumes of existing products and early traction in manufacturing and logistics offerings. FY26 revenue about Rs 316 crore, up 3% YoY.

segments.name: Customer Support Services (CSS)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue about Rs 37 crore, up 6% QoQ. FY26 revenue about Rs 113 crore, up 13% YoY, driven by new customers in infra-management (IMS) and solar-management services; solar managed base rose from 1 GW to 3 GW.

segments.name: EMS (within CSS, per call)
segments.commentary: External-customer revenue started in FY26 from the new Tumakuru SMT lines; utilisation is 30-40% and management expects it to rise in FY27. Sub-segment revenue not disclosed.

guidance_outlook: Company policy is not to give specific guidance; management said margin improvement is structural but quarterly volatility may continue.
Management said it is looking at double-digit revenue growth, though it declined to call growth in the higher single digits.
All three businesses (PSG, CSS, EMS) are expected to contribute to FY27 growth through new customers and deep selling.
Management expects the memory-price-driven order deferrals in PSG to fructify in FY27.
FY27 capex is business-as-usual plus tooling and moulds; Rs 40 crore already invested in expansion projects including the factory and EMS.
capex_capacity: Tumakuru (Karnataka) plant has new SMT lines for EMS; utilisation currently 30-40%, expected to rise in FY27.
Rs 40 crore invested so far across expansion projects (factory expansion and EMS).
FY27 capex plan is regular business-as-usual spend plus tools and moulds for new products; no quantum disclosed.

EMS focus is high-complexity, mid-volume products in auto, power electronics, industrial electronics and defence; management aims for EMS to eventually match PSG scale (roughly 50:50 mix), with no timeline given.
demand_pricing: Demand strong in BFSI and warehouse/logistics for product business; CSS growth from IT products and auto/power electronics.
Handheld devices and 2D scanners (AIDC) demand linked to manufacturing and logistics growth in India.

Memory and component price increases (management cited doubling or tripling in some cases) and supply-chain issues delayed PSG customer decisions; management expects customers to buy within one to two quarters.
Company deliberately exited some low-margin customers and orders, slowing revenue growth.
CSS authorised service partner network cut from 700+ in Q3 to 500+ in Q4 after exiting unprofitable remote geographies such as the Northeast.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margin reach 5.5-6%?
qa_highlights.answer: No formal guidance per company policy; management believes the margin gain is structural, though quarterly volatility may persist.

qa_highlights.question: Why did debt-to-equity rise to 0.43x?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher inventory to offset supply-chain and memory-price issues and slower customer collections, partly offset by better supplier payment terms; working capital minimum was raised.

qa_highlights.question: What is SMT line utilisation and anchor customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation 30-40%, with a few customers onboarded and more being added; expected to rise in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will EMS external revenue grow?
qa_highlights.answer: External revenue began in FY26; pipeline and prototype orders are expected to convert in FY27. Sub-segment revenue is not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Is growth in the higher single digits a safe assumption?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it expects robust overall growth and is looking at double-digit growth, not a repeat of the FY26 slowdown.

qa_highlights.question: What were the TCM initiatives?
qa_highlights.answer: Manpower, facility and other cost optimisation across businesses; management expects similar cost control to continue.

risks_watch: Memory and component cost inflation could delay PSG order conversion and push up product costs.
Working-capital intensity: debt-to-equity rose to 0.43x on inventory build and slower receivables.
EMS SMT utilisation at 30-40% means the new capacity is not yet earning its full returns; watch FY27 ramp.
Deliberate exit of low-margin customers and geographies may keep revenue growth below expectations.
No formal guidance and no sub-segment disclosure (EMS, e-auctions) limit tracking of progress.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margin structure and cost control, but cautious on near-term revenue, attributing PSG delays to memory pricing and customer deferrals. Management was evasive on timelines (EMS 50:50 mix, guidance) and declined to quantify sub-segment revenue.
key_quotes: we believe the margin improvement is structural rather than temporary, supported by the operational efficiencies and volume growth and disciplined execution.
Currently, the utilization is in the range of 30 % to 40% and we expect this to go up in the coming year.
So, long run, we don't see it will have an impact on our revenue growth.

adds.what: Tumakuru (Karnataka) SMT lines for EMS; external revenue started in FY26, utilisation 30-40%
Factory expansion (EMS and related), Rs 40 crore invested so far across expansion projects

growth.why: Management said it is looking at double-digit FY27 revenue growth with no range, backed by new customers across PSG, CSS and EMS, deferred PSG orders expected to fructify, and Tumakuru SMT lines running at 30-40% utilisation; no specific orders or contracts were quantified, so backing is vague.
